root_cause.text: Using bitfields for `claimed`, `can_retune`, `retune_now`, and `retune_paused` in `struct mmc_host` caused them to share the same machine word, so concurrent non-atomic read-modify-write updates to any of these fields could corrupt others, leading to spurious `WARN_ON(!host->claimed)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states "The host->claimed bit shared a word with retune flags. Writes to claimed in __mmc_claim_host() or retune_now in mmc_mq_queue_rq() can overwrite other bits when concurrent updates happen in other contexts, triggering spurious WARN_ON(!host->claimed)." The patch diff moves these fields from bitfields to separate `bool` variables to eliminate shared-word coupling.

vuln_statements.content: unsigned int		claimed:1;	/* host exclusively claimed */
unsigned int		can_retune:1;	/* re-tuning can be used */
unsigned int		retune_now:1;	/* do re-tuning at next req */
unsigned int		retune_paused:1;	/* re-tuning is temporarily disabled */

intent_record.what: In struct mmc_host, the bitfield 'claimed:1' is replaced with a separate 'bool claimed' member placed before the bitfield group, and the bitfields 'can_retune:1', 'retune_now:1', 'retune_paused:1' are removed entirely.
intent_record.how: The change turns the 'claimed' flag into a full bool variable (affecting memory layout and potential atomic access semantics), and eliminates three retune-related bitfields (removing their associated state tracking from the structure).

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boolean fields to mmc_host for more explicit re-tuning state management.
intent_record.what: Added three boolean fields (can_retune, retune_now, retune_paused) to the mmc_host structure, placed before the existing need_retune, hold_retune, and retune_period fields.
intent_record.how: These new fields enable the MMC core to explicitly track whether re-tuning is allowed (can_retune), whether re-tuning should be performed on the next request (retune_now), and whether re-tuning is temporarily paused (retune_paused). They provide more granular control over re-tuning behavior alongside the existing integer-based flags.
